public_rationale: All three named uses were documented before the post. In May 2024, OpenAI reported disrupting five covert influence operations that used its models to make deceptive political content. That covers misinformation. On 2024-12-03, the FBI warned that criminals use generative AI to commit fraud at larger scale. That covers scams. In October 2024, a Senate subcommittee investigation found that big Medicare Advantage insurers deployed AI and predictive tools, including NaviHealth's nH Predict, and that these tools generated more post-acute care denials. That covers insurance denials. UnitedHealth disputes that its tool makes coverage decisions. Still, the claim that AI 'has been used' in denying claims fits the Senate findings. The claim is about whether these uses occurred, not their scale or effect. OpenAI said the influence campaigns got little reach, and that does not change the result.
limitations: The insurance evidence comes through a secondary summary of the Senate report, because the primary PDF was blocked.
How far the insurer's AI tool itself decided denials is still disputed by UnitedHealth.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI has been used for misinformation, scams, and denying insurance claims.

statement.excerpt: He gives a long, flawed list of of AI positives but scarcely takes note of the negatives, like the way it has been used for misinformation, for scams, for denying insurance claims, and so on;
statement.document_title: Hard-forked! Casey Newton’s distorted portrait of Gary Marcus and AI skepticism

from_speaker: the way it has been used for misinformation
our_interpretation: Plain reading: by the post date (2024-12-06), there were documented real-world cases of AI being used in each of three ways: to produce or spread misinformation, to carry out scams, and to deny insurance claims.
The claim is about whether these uses happened. It is not about how common or how effective they were.
'AI' is read broadly to include generative AI and predictive algorithms, which is how the post uses the term.
Target period: Marcus names no period. I use 2019-01-01 to the post date, which covers the insurer algorithm deployments documented in 2019-2022 and the generative-AI misuse reported in 2023-2024.
criteria.support_condition: Credible primary or official sources, available by the evaluation date, document AI being used for (a) misinformation or influence campaigns, (b) fraud or scams, and (c) denying or driving denials of insurance claims, on or before 2024-12-06.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible investigation shows that one or more of the three named uses did not happen. For example, the insurer tools played no part in claim denials, or the reported AI misuse cases were fabricated.

evidence.excerpt: In the last three months, we have disrupted five covert IO that sought to use our models in support of deceptive activity across the internet.
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports that state-linked and commercial influence operations used its models to make deceptive political content. That is the misinformation use. OpenAI also says the campaigns gained little reach, but the claim is only that the use happened.

evidence.excerpt: The FBI is warning the public that criminals exploit generative artificial intelligence (AI) to commit fraud on a larger scale which increases the believability of their schemes.
evidence.explanation: An official FBI advisory, issued three days before the post, says criminals use generative AI for fraud. That is the scams use.

evidence.excerpt: the report documents these plans testing and deploying a series of artificial intelligence, automation and/or predictive technology tools. The result was most of these tools generated more denials.
evidence.locator: Key Findings, AI and predictive technologies section
evidence.explanation: This summarizes the October 2024 Senate subcommittee report. It found that the large Medicare Advantage insurers deployed AI and predictive tools that produced more denials of post-acute care in 2019-2022. That is the insurance-denial use.

evidence.excerpt: UnitedHealth denied all claims that nH Predict is used for coverage determinations, according to HealthCare Drive.
